instruction.text:
Listen to Henry’s thoughts about choosing what to eat for lunch. Are they good reasons for pizza or good reasons for pasta?
Drag them to the correct group.

atoms.sound: Pizza is my favourite food. I love pizza!
I would have to do less dishes after making pizza. If I cook pasta, I’ll need to wash all the pots and pans by hand.
My aunt brought back some spaghetti from her holiday to Italy. I really want to know if it tastes better than the pasta I usually buy.

instruction.text: Select which choice Henry should make based on his reasons.
Now Henry has to choose what to put on the pizza. Listen to Henry’s thoughts and drag them to the correct group.

atoms.sound: Pizza is not that healthy to begin with, so I probably shouldn’t put extra cheese on it. I should stick with vegetables instead.
I love how colourful the different vegetables look on my pizza.

instruction.text: Select which choice Henry should make based on his reasons.
Nolan’s class is fighting over whether to go to the museum or the zoo for their school trip. Listen and select the correct way to solve the problem.

b.sound: Nolan suggests taking a vote. His classmates agree that this is the best way to make a choice as a group.
Nolan starts throwing paper at his classmates who want to go to the museum. He really wants to go to the zoo.

instruction.text: The class wants to vote secretly. How should they do that? Listen and select the correct answer.

b.sound: Each pupil should write either 'zoo' or 'museum' on a piece of paper and put it in a bowl on the teacher’s desk. The votes will then be counted.
When asked about where they would rather go, they should raise their hands for either the zoo or the museum.

instruction.text: The votes were counted in a tally chart. Select the side that got more votes.

text: That’s decided then! The class is going to the zoo.
